correctness.rationale: Stationary generator on distinct squared-coordinate products gives \(M_k=(2D/r)^k\,k!/(q_1\cdots q_k)\) for k<=3, with q_k the hypergeometric probability of reset intersection. Substituting these exact moments gives V_N(m); all positive-denominator algebra has been checked symbolically. The difference V_N(3)-V_N(m) is factored as (m-3)B times an explicitly positive prefactor; four small-m substitutions and a two-variable (m-8,N-m-2) expansion have strictly positive integer coefficients and cover all \(4\le m\le N-2\) for \(N\ge10\). An exact positive polynomial compares m=3 with m=N-1, while a quadratic with its larger root strictly between 73 and 74 decides m=2 vs m=3. Exhaustive exact rational comparisons cover \(3\le N\le9\). verify.py reconstructs the identities and tests \(N\le150\) independently; the unbounded result rests on coefficient positivity, not finite tests.

originality.rationale: The first 2026 article derives the model and an exact general marginal recursion, and explicitly optimizes its pair connected covariance with a single population threshold (\(N=6\)). Its complete HTML including supplemental sections was examined for this specific three-distinct-label squared-displacement cumulant and integer global maximizers. The published all-order moment closure may imply the intermediate three-particle moment formulas, and that arithmetic derivation is not claimed novel. The complete all-N *optimization* for the third connected cumulant, especially its distinct \(N=10\) and \(N=74\) transitions and exact uniqueness, was not found or implied by a stated stronger result in the examined sources. An independently sourced 2026 survey emphasizes the pair-level phenomenon. Direct published-finding corpus semantic searches of source, object, cumulant, aliases, and threshold returned semantically unrelated nearest findings (IDs recorded), with no stronger covering result. The residual possibility of undiscovered unindexed or implicit optimization remains.

value.rationale: The third distinct-particle connected cumulant measures irreducible three-body fluctuations in a collective reset gas, not merely pairwise covariance. The source establishes a first-order (pair) optimizer transition. A complete classification of the natural next connected cumulant yields two unexpected optimizer transitions \(N=10\) and \(N=74\), proves the optimal batch is never 1 or N, and gives unique maximizers for every physically meaningful integer \(N\ge3\). The result has a motivated physical observable, sharp natural finite-population cutoffs and future use for selecting batch protocols that amplify higher connected correlations; it is not a one-off numerical example or unmotivated narrow invariant.
